nuggets.title: Launch Day Transcode Backlog Blocks New 4K Titles

scenario.symptoms: Major series premiere shows 'format unavailable' on TV apps for 6 hours. Transcode queue depth exceeds 50k jobs while only SD renditions exist.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Single FIFO transcode pool without priority for launch titles or pre-warming; mezzanine uploaded 30 minutes before go-live.

incident.headline: Under-provisioned transcoding with no launch priority leaves premiere titles undeliverable

agenda.goal: Scale transcoding with priority lanes, pre-warm before release, and parallel profiles per title.
agenda.opener: Our big premiere wasn't playable in 4K for hours because transcodes weren't ready. How does transcoding keep up with catalog and launches?

evidence.strong: Priority queues for launch windows, autoscale transcode fleet, pre-transcode mezzanine early, parallel ladder generation, SLA alerts on queue depth.
evidence.weak: On-demand transcode at playback time only.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes transcode can always happen at play click.
misconceptions.challenge: Can you generate all ABR rungs in seconds at request time?

probes: When must mezzanine arrive before release?
Which renditions are mandatory at go-live?
agenda.referenceFix: Launch priority queue, pre-scale workers, block go-live until required rungs exist.

nuggets.title: ABR Algorithm Oscillates Quality on Live Sports

scenario.symptoms: Live match viewers see quality ping-pong between 1080p and 360p every 10 seconds with frequent rebuffering on stable 50 Mbps links.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Player uses throughput-only ABR without buffer occupancy target; CDN token bucket throttling misread as network drop.

incident.headline: Naive throughput-based ABR causes quality oscillation and rebuffer on live streams

agenda.goal: Use buffer-based ABR with hysteresis, live latency target, and CDN-aware throughput estimation.
agenda.opener: Viewers on fast Wi-Fi still see quality bouncing during live sports. How does your player pick bitrates?

evidence.strong: Buffer occupancy target (BOLA/LL), hysteresis to prevent oscillation, separate live ladder, cap max ramp speed, consider segment download time variance.
evidence.adequate: Throughput estimate with fixed safety margin only.
evidence.weak: Always max quality until buffer empty.

misconceptions.pattern: Uses last segment throughput as sole signal.
misconceptions.challenge: What if CDN briefly delivers faster than sustainable rate?

probes: How do you handle live low-latency targets?
hints: Buffer level predicts stalls better than last throughput.
agenda.referenceFix: Buffer-based ABR with live-tuned parameters and oscillation damping.

nuggets.title: Cache Miss Storm Melts Origin During Viral Clip

scenario.symptoms: Viral clip triggers 900 Gbps origin egress; origin error rate 40% while edges show low hit ratio on new URL variants with unique query params.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Players request segments with per-session cache-busting query strings preventing CDN cache key reuse.

incident.headline: Cache key fragmentation causes thundering herd on origin during viral traffic

agenda.goal: Maximize edge hit ratio with stable cache keys, prefetch, shield origin, and signed URLs without busting cache.
agenda.opener: A viral clip melted our origin despite having a CDN. Why weren't segments cached at the edge?

evidence.strong: Cache-friendly URLs, strip auth to cookie/header, origin shield, prefetch hot titles, tiered storage near origin, monitor hit ratio per title.
evidence.adequate: CDN enabled but unique query params per user.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes adding CDN guarantees cache hits.
misconceptions.challenge: If every URL is unique, what is the hit ratio?

probes: What belongs in cache key vs auth header?
How do you warm cache for a launch?
hints: Auth should not fragment segment keys.
agenda.referenceFix: Normalize cache keys, signed cookies, prefetch viral content, alert on hit ratio drop.

nuggets.title: Missing QoE Beacons Blind Playback Failure Analysis

scenario.symptoms: Support hears playback complaints but dashboards show 99.9% success. Client QoE beacons dropped on ad blocker and batch flush failures during background mobile.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Analytics relies on client-side batch POST without server-side CDN log correlation or session heartbeat.

incident.headline: Client-only QoE pipeline under-reports playback failures visible to users

agenda.goal: Measure QoE with reliable beacons plus CDN/server logs joined by session id.
agenda.opener: Users complain about buffering but metrics look fine. How do you know real playback quality?

evidence.strong: Dual collection client+CDN, session id in URLs, retry beacons, RUM sampling, rebuffer and startup metrics, join in warehouse.

misconceptions.pattern: Equates segment HTTP 200 with good UX.
misconceptions.challenge: Can player stall while segments return 200?

probes: Which metrics define a bad session?
hints: Session id links client and edge.
agenda.referenceFix: Join client QoE with CDN access logs; alert on rebuffer rate not just errors.

scenario.symptoms: Monthly CDN egress bill jumps 35% after UI change defaults mobile autoplay to highest rung. Most phones never switch down on cellular.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Player starts at top bitrate in ladder without data-saver policy or device-aware cap.

incident.headline: Aggressive default bitrate selection inflates CDN egress without quality benefit on small screens

agenda.goal: Control cost with device-aware defaults, capped ladders, and efficient codecs while preserving QoE targets.
agenda.opener: CDN costs spiked after we defaulted everyone to 4K on mobile. How do you balance quality and egress spend?

evidence.strong: Start on middle rung, cap cellular bitrate, AV1/HEVC where supported, per-title encoding optimization, data saver setting, monitor cost per stream hour.
evidence.adequate: ABR without caps relies on algorithm alone.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes highest bitrate always means better UX on mobile.
misconceptions.challenge: Can users see 4K on a 6-inch screen?

probes: How does codec choice affect bill?
agenda.referenceFix: Cellular-aware defaults, optimized ladders, monitor egress per cohort.
